newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court maintains frozen beef quota system for newcomers.
newsitem.headline: Court maintains frozen beef quota system for newcomers.

text.p: The European Court of Justice upheld on Thursday the European Commission regulation detailing rules on imports for frozen beef.
Aeerington Beef of Britain made an unsuccessful bid to overturn quotas imposed under a system which distinguishes between newcomers and traditional importers.
The newcomers' quota is allocated in proportion to quantities applied for, rather than in proportion to imports or exports in past reference years as with traditional importers.
The court noted that the eligibility criteria for quotas were comparable between newcomers and traditional importers, and Aeerington's plea of discrimination was rejected.

"The reasons for restricting cumulation to traditional importers who are already eligible derive clearly and unequivocally from the conditions for access to the quota and its allocations between the eligible traders," the court said.
"Frozen beef - Common import rules - Community tariff quotas - Newcomers"

Consideration in the light of the grounds stated in the order for reference of articles 1(2) and 2(2) of Commission regulation (EC) No 214/94 of 31 January 1994 laying down detailed rules for the application of Council regulation (EC) No 130/94 with regard to the import arrangements for frozen beef falling within CN code 0202 and products falling within CN code 0206 29 91 has disclosed no factor capable of affecting their validity.
